objects.description: Basic byte type used to transmit all character fields. Only defined here when TPM_HAVE_TPM2_DECLARATIONS is not set.
Boolean byte used for TRUE/FALSE fields in TPM APIs. TRUE = 0x01, FALSE = 0x00. Separate from Windows BOOL.
Byte enum-like type indicating when authorization must be presented. Actual values not defined here.
Byte indicating what the payload is in an encrypted structure. Specific values not defined here.
Byte representing a component of a TPM version field.
Byte indicating state of dictionary attack mitigation logic.
Low byte of TPM_ENTITY_TYPE, representing entity type details. Values not defined here.
High byte of TPM_ENTITY_TYPE indicating ADIP encryption scheme. Values not defined here.
Identifier of the TPM protocol in use.
Indicates the TPM start state.
Encryption scheme identifier.
Signature scheme identifier.
Migration scheme identifier.
Represents state of physical presence mechanism.
Indicates types of entities supported by the TPM.
Permitted usage flags for a key.
Type of asymmetric encrypted structure used by the Endorsement Key (EK).
Tag indicating the structure type in serialized forms.
Identifier of the platform-specific spec to which data relates.
Command ordinal code for TPM commands.
Identifier of a TPM capability area.
Bitfield indicating properties of a key.
Algorithm identifier. Only defined here when TPM_HAVE_TPM2_DECLARATIONS is not set.
Locality modifier value. Only defined here when TPM_HAVE_TPM2_DECLARATIONS is not set.
Actual counter value for a monotonic counter.
Attributes controlling options in a transport session.
Handle to an authorization session.
Index into a DIR register.
Handle referencing a TPM-held key.
Index of a PCR register.
TPM return code type for command results.
Enumerates internal TPM resource types.
Controls key handling when loaded and startup behaviors.
Index into non-volatile (NV) storage. Only defined when TPM_HAVE_TPM2_DECLARATIONS is not set.
Identifier for an authorization family, assigned by the TPM.
Label for most recent verification of a family; zero when unused.
Flags indicating TPM handling on startup.
Mode for symmetric encryption operations.
Family flags associated with authorization families.
Index value into the delegate NV table.
Restrictions placed on delegation of Certified Migration Key (CMK) commands.
Identifier of a monotonic counter instance.
Command identifier to execute in restricted edit contexts. Specifics not defined here.
Handle for a transport session.
Generic handle type (key, transport, etc.). Only defined when TPM_HAVE_TPM2_DECLARATIONS is not set.
Operation code indicating the family-related operation in progress.
Tag for TPM command and response headers (noted as not in specification section).
Abstract handle/pointer to a symmetric key token; represented as a pointer to bytes. Allocation/ownership not defined here.
Abstract big-number representation as a pointer to bytes. Size, encoding, and lifetime are unspecified here.
No custom data types are defined in this header. It only defines a set of preprocessor macros (#define) for TPM error/return codes. There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes to extract.
No custom data types (structs, enums, typedefs, or classes) are defined in this header. The file only defines string macros for NVRAM file base names.

Status/result code type used by the TPM I/O API functions declared in this header. It is only referenced here; its actual definition is not present in this header and is presumably provided by tpm_types.h.

Boolean type used by the TPM I/O API, specifically for reporting TPM establishment state. It is only referenced here; its actual definition is not present in this header and is presumably provided by tpm_types.h.

TPM_RESULT is referenced as the return type of the allocation APIs but is not defined in this header. It is presumably an enum or typedef declared in tpm_types.h representing TPM return/status codes. No definition present here.

uint32_t is referenced as a parameter type but is not defined in this header; it is typically a standard fixed-width integer typedef likely provided by tpm_types.h or stdint.h. No definition present here.

unsigned char is a built-in type used for raw byte buffers in the allocation APIs. It is not defined in this header; included here only because it appears as a parameter type. No custom type definition exists here.
Enumerates TPM implementation versions that libtpms can operate as (TPM 1.2 or TPM 2.0). Used with TPMLIB_ChooseTPMVersion.

objects.definition:
enum TPMLIB_TPMProperty {

objects.description: Enumeration of queryable TPM implementation properties for TPMLIB_GetTPMProperty. Values start at 1 and auto-increment.
Bitmask flags controlling what informational strings TPMLIB_GetInfo should return about the TPM implementation and runtime state.

Callback vtable provided by the embedding application to supply NVRAM persistence and I/O related services to libtpms. sizeOfStruct must be set by caller for versioning. Function pointers are invoked by libtpms; implementers must obey the signatures and allocation semantics (e.g., tpm_nvram_loaddata allocates and returns data).
Enumeration of blob types understood by TPMLIB_DecodeBlob; currently only INITSTATE is defined. TPMLIB_BLOB_TYPE_LAST is a sentinel.
Bitmask identifying TPM state sections (permanent, volatile, and save-state). Used with state validation, set, and get APIs. May be combined as flags.

functions.name: TPM_IO_Hash_Start
functions.description: Begins a streaming hash operation within the TPM TIS I/O layer. Typically used as the first step before feeding data with TPM_IO_Hash_Data and finalizing with TPM_IO_Hash_End. The specific hash algorithm and scope are not documented here; the context is managed internally by this module.
requirements: Must be called before TPM_IO_Hash_Data and TPM_IO_Hash_End for a given hashing sequence.
Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT and abort the hashing sequence on failure.
Not thread-safety- or reentrancy-guaranteed by this header; concurrent use is unknown.

functions.name: TPM_IO_Hash_Data
functions.signature: TPM_RESULT TPM_IO_Hash_Data(const unsigned char *data, uint32_t data_length);
functions.description: Feeds a chunk of data into the currently active hash operation started by TPM_IO_Hash_Start. May be used to stream data in multiple calls before finalizing with TPM_IO_Hash_End. The exact hashing details are not specified in this header.
requirements: TPM_IO_Hash_Start must have succeeded before calling this function.
The pointer 'data' must reference at least 'data_length' bytes of readable memory when data_length > 0.
May be called multiple times between TPM_IO_Hash_Start and TPM_IO_Hash_End to stream additional data (inferred from naming).
Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT and handle errors; subsequent calls may be invalid if an error occurs.

functions.name: TPM_IO_Hash_End
functions.description: Finalizes the current hash operation that was started with TPM_IO_Hash_Start and fed via TPM_IO_Hash_Data. Closes the internal hashing context. Any resulting digest handling (if applicable) is not exposed by this interface and is unknown from this header.
requirements: TPM_IO_Hash_Start must have been successfully called prior to this call.
Should be called after all intended TPM_IO_Hash_Data calls have completed.
Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT and handle errors.
Behavior if called without a matching TPM_IO_Hash_Start is undefined from this header and should be avoided.

functions.name: TPM_IO_TpmEstablished_Get
functions.description: Queries the TPM ‘establishment’ state via the TIS I/O layer and returns it in tpmEstablished. This typically reflects whether a TPM establishment event/condition has occurred. Exact semantics of the flag are not described in this header.
requirements: The pointer 'tpmEstablished' must be non-NULL and writable.
Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT; on success, '*tpmEstablished' is set to a boolean value.
No specific initialization or prior calls are stated as required in this header.

functions.name: TPM_IO_TpmEstablished_Reset
functions.description: Attempts to reset/clear the TPM ‘establishment’ indication through the TIS I/O layer. The precise conditions, privileges, or platform requirements to perform this reset are not documented here and may depend on the environment.
requirements: Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT to determine if the reset succeeded.
May require platform or privilege conditions not specified in this header; availability is unknown.

functions.name: TPM_Malloc
functions.description: Allocates a memory block of the requested size and returns it via buffer, using TPM-specific status codes (TPM_RESULT). Intended as a bounded wrapper around malloc; allocation is limited by TPM_ALLOC_MAX (128 KiB) to prevent resource overuse. On success, *buffer points to a writable block of size bytes; on failure, a non-success TPM_RESULT is returned and *buffer is unspecified/likely unchanged. Exact error codes are unknown without tpm_types.h.
requirements: buffer must be a non-NULL pointer to a caller-provided unsigned char* variable that can receive the allocated pointer (inferred from double-pointer signature).
size should be less than or equal to TPM_ALLOC_MAX (0x20000) as allocation is limited to prevent resource overload (explicitly stated by the header comment and macro).
Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT for success before using *buffer (inferred from status-returning signature).
On success, the caller owns the returned memory and must release it with TPM_Free (inferred from naming and API pattern).
Behavior when size is 0 is unspecified in this header; callers should avoid passing size == 0 or handle implementation-defined behavior (not documented).
Returned memory alignment and initialization state are unspecified; assume uninitialized like malloc (inferred).

functions.name: TPM_Realloc
functions.description: Changes the size of a previously allocated memory block referenced by *buffer and returns the (possibly moved) pointer via buffer, using TPM_RESULT status. Acts as a bounded wrapper around realloc with an allocation cap of TPM_ALLOC_MAX (128 KiB). If size is larger than the cap or allocation fails, a non-success TPM_RESULT is returned. Exact error codes are unknown without tpm_types.h.
requirements: buffer must be a non-NULL pointer to an unsigned char* that either points to a block previously obtained from TPM_Malloc/TPM_Realloc or is NULL to request a fresh allocation (inferred from realloc semantics and API pattern).
size should be less than or equal to TPM_ALLOC_MAX (0x20000) due to the stated allocation limit (explicitly stated by the header comment and macro).
Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT for success before using *buffer (inferred from status-returning signature).
On success, the caller owns the returned memory and must later release it with TPM_Free (inferred from naming and API pattern).
If the function fails, the state of *buffer is unspecified by this header; callers should not assume it is unchanged (standard realloc may leave original pointer intact or not—unspecified here).
Behavior when size is 0 is unspecified in this header; callers should avoid size == 0 or handle implementation-defined behavior (not documented).

functions.name: TPM_Free
functions.description: Releases a memory block previously returned by TPM_Malloc or TPM_Realloc. This is a wrapper around free with TPM-specific allocation lifecycle. It does not return a status code; any error handling behavior is unknown from this header.
requirements: buffer should be either NULL (no effect, typical but not guaranteed) or a pointer previously returned by TPM_Malloc/TPM_Realloc and not already freed (inferred from free semantics and API pattern).
After calling TPM_Free, the buffer pointer becomes invalid; callers should not dereference it and should set their variable to NULL to avoid use-after-free (inferred).
Thread-safety and double-free behavior are unspecified in this header; callers must avoid double freeing (inferred).

functions.name: TPMLIB_GetVersion
functions.description: Returns the libtpms interface/library version encoded via TPM_LIBRARY_VERSION_GEN(MAJ, MIN, MICRO). Use to check ABI/version compatibility at runtime.
requirements: No arguments.
Caller should compare against TPM_LIBRARY_VERSION or decode fields via bit shifts.

functions.name: TPMLIB_ChooseTPMVersion
functions.description: Selects which TPM implementation version (1.2 or 2.0) the library should use before initialization.
requirements: Must be called before TPMLIB_MainInit and before any stateful TPM operation.
Parameter ver must be one of TPMLIB_TPM_VERSION_1_2 or TPMLIB_TPM_VERSION_2.
Subsequent calls may be undefined; behavior for re-selection is unknown.

functions.name: TPMLIB_MainInit
functions.description: Initializes the TPM library and internal emulator state. Call once before processing commands or accessing TPM state.
requirements: Should be called exactly once per process lifetime before TPMLIB_Process, TPMLIB_GetState/SetState, etc.
Prior to initialization, callbacks (e.g., NV storage, I/O) may need registration via TPMLIB_RegisterCallbacks if used by the chosen profile; exact requirements are unknown.
Check returned TPM_RESULT for errors.

functions.name: TPMLIB_Terminate
functions.description: Shuts down the TPM library and releases internal resources.
requirements: Call after finishing with the library, typically once, and not concurrently with TPMLIB_Process.
Do not use other TPMLIB_* functions that require an initialized TPM after termination.

functions.name: TPMLIB_Process
functions.signature: TPM_RESULT TPMLIB_Process(unsigned char **respbuffer, uint32_t *resp_size, uint32_t *respbufsize, unsigned char *command, uint32_t command_size);
functions.description: Processes a single TPM command buffer and returns the TPM response buffer. Manages/returns the response buffer via respbuffer/resp_size/respbufsize.
requirements: TPMLIB_MainInit must have succeeded prior to calling.
respbuffer, resp_size, and respbufsize must be valid, writable pointers.
command must point to a buffer of length command_size.
command_size must match the actual command buffer length; zero-length commands are invalid for TPM.
Ownership and lifetime of *respbuffer is unknown from this header; caller should not assume stack allocation and should follow library documentation for freeing or reuse.
Not thread-safe unless documented elsewhere; avoid concurrent calls without external synchronization.

functions.name: TPMLIB_VolatileAll_Store
functions.description: Serializes all current volatile TPM state into a binary blob returned via buffer/buflen. Useful for checkpointing volatile state.
requirements: TPMLIB_MainInit must have succeeded.
buffer and buflen must be valid, writable pointers.
Returned buffer ownership and required deallocation routine are unknown; consult implementation to avoid leaks.

functions.name: TPMLIB_CancelCommand
functions.description: Requests cancellation of a currently running TPM command, if supported by the active backend/profile.
requirements: Should only be called when a command is in flight; otherwise behavior/result is implementation-defined.
Caller must check the returned TPM_RESULT to determine whether cancellation was honored.

functions.name: TPMLIB_GetTPMProperty
functions.description: Queries static limits or capacities of the TPM implementation (e.g., buffer sizes, handle counts) and returns the value via result.
requirements: prop must be one of enum TPMLIB_TPMProperty values.
result must be a valid, writable pointer to int.
May require TPMLIB_MainInit depending on property; not specified here.

functions.name: TPMLIB_GetInfo
functions.description: Returns informational text about the TPM emulator and runtime, controlled by bitwise flags (specification, attributes, features, algorithms, commands, profiles, runtime attributes).
requirements: flags must be a bitwise OR of TPMLIB_INFO_* values.
Returned char* ownership and lifetime are unknown from this header; caller must consult documentation before freeing or storing the pointer.

functions.name: TPMLIB_RegisterCallbacks
functions.description: Registers host-provided callback functions for NVRAM and I/O integration used by the TPM library.
requirements: The argument must be a valid pointer to struct libtpms_callbacks stored object.
sizeOfStruct should be set to sizeof(struct libtpms_callbacks) (common pattern for versioning).
Each provided function pointer must be valid for the lifetime of the library use; unset/NULL callbacks may limit available functionality depending on profile.
Should be called before TPMLIB_MainInit so the TPM can use these services during initialization and operation.

functions.name: TPMLIB_DecodeBlob
functions.signature: TPM_RESULT TPMLIB_DecodeBlob(const char *data, enum TPMLIB_BlobType type, unsigned char **result, size_t *result_len);
functions.description: Parses and decodes an ASCII-armored blob (e.g., INITSTATE delimited by TPMLIB_INITSTATE_*_TAG) into a binary buffer.
requirements: data must point to a NUL-terminated string containing the encoded blob of the specified type.
type must be a valid enum TPMLIB_BlobType (e.g., TPMLIB_BLOB_TYPE_INITSTATE).
result and result_len must be valid, writable pointers; on success they receive the allocated binary data and length.
Ownership and deallocation method for *result is unspecified here; consult implementation for how to free it.
Input must include correct BEGIN/END tags for the given type.

functions.name: TPMLIB_SetDebugFD
functions.description: Sets the file descriptor used for libtpms debug output/logging.
requirements: fd should be a valid, open file descriptor suitable for write operations.
May be called before other functions to capture early logs.

functions.name: TPMLIB_SetDebugLevel
functions.description: Sets verbosity of libtpms debug logging to the specified level.
requirements: level range/meaning is not defined in this header; callers should use documented levels.
Can be called at runtime to adjust logging.

functions.name: TPMLIB_SetDebugPrefix
functions.description: Sets a string prefix applied to debug log messages for identification.
requirements: prefix must be a valid pointer to a NUL-terminated string; empty string is allowed though effect is implementation-defined.
Caller should check the returned TPM_RESULT for validation errors (e.g., overly long prefix).

functions.name: TPMLIB_SetBufferSize
functions.description: Requests a TPM internal command/response buffer size and reports the allowed minimum and maximum. Returns the effective size selected.
requirements: wanted_size should be a positive value; zero or too-small values may be clamped to min.
If provided, min_size and max_size must be writable pointers; they may be NULL if the caller does not need the values (not specified, but common pattern).
Must be called before operations that depend on TPM buffer sizing; exact timing relative to initialization is unspecified.

functions.name: TPMLIB_ValidateState
functions.signature: TPM_RESULT TPMLIB_ValidateState(enum TPMLIB_StateType st, unsigned int flags);
functions.description: Validates that a provided state blob (of the indicated type) would be acceptable to the TPM, or checks current state against criteria indicated by flags. Exact semantics are not documented here.
requirements: st must be a bitmask composed of TPMLIB_STATE_PERMANENT, TPMLIB_STATE_VOLATILE, and/or TPMLIB_STATE_SAVE_STATE.
flags meaning is unspecified in this header; pass 0 if unsure or follow external documentation.
Must be called with a properly initialized library if it inspects current state.

functions.name: TPMLIB_SetState
functions.signature: TPM_RESULT TPMLIB_SetState(enum TPMLIB_StateType st, const unsigned char *buffer, uint32_t buflen);
functions.description: Loads TPM state of the specified type from a caller-provided binary blob into the emulator.
requirements: TPMLIB_MainInit should have succeeded before loading state unless documented otherwise.
st must specify exactly one or a valid combination of TPMLIB_STATE_* types expected by the buffer content.
buffer must be non-NULL if buflen > 0 and must point to at least buflen bytes.
buflen must match the size of the serialized state; passing mismatched data may return errors or be rejected by TPMLIB_ValidateState first.

functions.name: TPMLIB_GetState
functions.signature: TPM_RESULT TPMLIB_GetState(enum TPMLIB_StateType st, unsigned char **buffer, uint32_t *buflen);
functions.description: Exports the current TPM state of the specified type into an allocated binary blob returned via buffer/buflen.
requirements: TPMLIB_MainInit must have succeeded.
st must be one of the TPMLIB_STATE_* flags or a valid combination if supported.
buffer and buflen must be valid, writable pointers.
Ownership and deallocation method for *buffer are unspecified here; consult implementation to free correctly.

functions.name: TPMLIB_SetProfile
functions.description: Selects or activates a named TPM profile (capability set/configuration) for the emulator.
requirements: profile must be a valid, NUL-terminated string naming an available profile.
Should be called before initialization or before operations depending on the profile; timing rules are not specified here.
Caller must check the return value for invalid/unknown profile errors.

functions.name: TPMLIB_WasManufactured
functions.description: Indicates whether the TPM has undergone its manufacturing/initialization process (i.e., has valid permanent state).
requirements: No arguments.
Call after initialization to get a meaningful result; semantics before init are unspecified.

data_types.description: An arbitrary byte sequence with no required encoding or character constraints. May contain any 0x00–0xFF values and is treated as opaque binary input.
A NUL-terminated string comprised primarily of printable ASCII characters (0x20–0x7E) possibly including newlines and other ASCII control characters. Used where APIs expect textual input.

A textual, ASCII-style armored encoding that includes explicit BEGIN and END tags surrounding payload content (e.g., headers and base64-like body). The content is decoded into a binary buffer if tags and structure match the expected blob type.
A NUL-terminated string intended to be valid UTF-8 text. Can include any Unicode code points encoded per UTF-8; used for human-readable names, prefixes, or identifiers.

generators.generator:
import random
import struct
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for raw binary data tailored to libtpms fuzzing stubs that consume:
# - TPM_IO_Hash_Data: arbitrary byte chunks (can be empty too)
# - TPMLIB_Process: TPM command buffers (non-empty, <= 2048 bytes)
# - TPMLIB_SetState: serialized state blobs for PERMANENT/VOLATILE/SAVE_STATE (opaque to us)
#
# Strategy:
# - Produce a buffer that is likely a valid TPM command for TPMLIB_Process to accept.
#   TPM 1.2/2.0 commands start with a header: tag (2 bytes), length (4 bytes BE), ordinal (4 bytes)
#   For 1.2: tag often 0x00C1 (auth1) or 0x00C2 (auth2) or 0x00C1/0x00C2/0x00C1; 0x00C1 is common.
#   For 2.0: tag 0x8001 (sessions), 0x8002 (no sessions); code sizes are also BE.
#   We will craft multiple plausible headers and choose one, then pad parameters with random bytes.
# - Keep total size <= 2048.
# - Sometimes generate small or empty buffers suitable for TPM_IO_Hash_Data and TPMLIB_SetState.
# - Ensure header length field matches actual buffer size for the TPMLIB_Process path.
#
# The fuzzer framework will feed this once as FUZZ_PARAM_STR or to files; we provide one blob that is
# a valid TPM command by default to drive TPMLIB_Process, while still being arbitrary binary if used elsewhere.

TPM12_COMMON_ORDINALS = [
    0x00000065,  # TPM_Startup
    0x0000000C,  # TPM_GetRandom
    0x0000007A,  # TPM_Extend (1.2)
    0x000000CF,  # TPM_ForceClear
    0x00000053,  # TPM_ReadPubek
    0x00000097,  # TPM_PcrRead
]

TPM20_COMMON_CC = [
    0x00000144,  # TPM2_Startup
    0x0000017B,  # TPM2_GetRandom
    0x0000017E,  # TPM2_PCR_Read
    0x00000126,  # TPM2_Clear
    0x00000131,  # TPM2_ReadPublic
]


def _be16(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">H", x & 0xFFFF)


def _be32(x: int) -> bytes:
    return struct.pack(">I", x & 0xFFFFFFFF)


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _build_tpm12_command(rng: random.Random, max_size: int) -> bytes:
    # Choose a tag: 0x00C1 (auth1), 0x00C2 (auth2), or 0x0001 (no auth, rare but appears)
    tag = rng.choice([0x00C1, 0x00C2, 0x0001])
    ordinal = rng.choice(TPM12_COMMON_ORDINALS)

    # Create a parameter body that matches the ordinal style minimally.
    # For GetRandom (0x0C), parameter is size (u32) requested bytes.
    if ordinal == 0x0000000C:
        req_len = rng.randint(1, 64)
        params = _be32(req_len)
    # For Startup (0x65) param is TPM_STARTUP_TYPE u16 (0x0001 or 0x0002 typical). Provide common values.
    elif ordinal == 0x00000065:
        st = rng.choice([0x0001, 0x0002])
        params = _be16(st)
    # For PCRRead (0x97), parameters include PCR index u32; choose 0..23
    elif ordinal == 0x00000097:
        pcr = rng.randint(0, 23)
        params = _be32(pcr)
    # For Extend (0x7A), params: PCR index u32 + 20-byte digest
    elif ordinal == 0x0000007A:
        pcr = rng.randint(0, 23)
        params = _be32(pcr) + _rand_bytes(rng, 20)
    # For ReadPubek (0x53) no params
    elif ordinal == 0x00000053:
        params = b""
    # For ForceClear (0xCF) no params
    elif ordinal == 0x000000CF:
        params = b""
    else:
        params = b""

    # If tag indicates sessions (auth), append a minimal authorization area-ish blob.
    if tag in (0x00C1, 0x00C2):
        # Minimal single authorization: handle (u32), nonceEven(20), nonceOdd(20), contAuth(u8), auth(20)
        # This is synthetic but structured; size expectations vary across commands, but many accept it.
        auth_area = (
            _be32(rng.randrange(0, 0xFFFFFFFF))
            + _rand_bytes(rng, 20)
            + _rand_bytes(rng, 20)
            + bytes([rng.randrange(0, 2)])
            + _rand_bytes(rng, 20)
        )
        params += auth_area

    # Assemble header: tag(2) + size(4) + ordinal(4)
    header_wo_len = _be16(tag) + b"\x00\x00\x00\x00" + _be32(ordinal)
    total_len = 2 + 4 + 4 + len(params)
    if total_len > max_size:
        # Trim params if needed
        trim = total_len - max_size
        if trim >= len(params):
            params = b""
        else:
            params = params[:-trim]
        total_len = 2 + 4 + 4 + len(params)
    header = _be16(tag) + _be32(total_len) + _be32(ordinal)
    return header + params


def _build_tpm20_command(rng: random.Random, max_size: int) -> bytes:
    # TPM2 header: tag(2): 0x8001 (sessions) or 0x8002 (no sessions)
    tag = rng.choice([0x8001, 0x8002])
    cc = rng.choice(TPM20_COMMON_CC)

    # Build command-specific parameters
    if cc == 0x0000017B:  # GetRandom: bytesRequested u16
        req_len = rng.randint(1, 64)
        params = _be16(req_len)
    elif cc == 0x00000144:  # Startup: TPM_SU u16 (0x0000 or 0x0001 typically)
        params = _be16(rng.choice([0x0000, 0x0001]))
    elif cc == 0x0000017E:  # PCR_Read: TPML_PCR_SELECTION; provide minimal, 1 selection of bank SHA1/bitmask
        # count(4 bytes? Actually TPM2 marshals count u32 for TPML_*, but PCR selection uses u32 count then list)
        # Use a minimal encoding: count=1(u32), hashAlg=0x0004(SHA1)(u16), sizeOfSelect=3(u8), select[3] bitmask
        pcr_index = rng.randint(0, 23)
        byte = 1 << (pcr_index % 8)
        select = byte.to_bytes(1, 'big') + b"\x00\x00"
        params = _be32(1) + _be16(0x0004) + bytes([3]) + select
    elif cc == 0x00000126:  # Clear: requires auth handle etc.; supply minimal handles and sessions
        # Handles: auth handle (u32) in handle area; we'll use TPM_RH_LOCKOUT=0x4000000A or owner=0x40000001
        handle = rng.choice([0x4000000A, 0x40000001])
        handles = _be32(handle)
        if tag == 0x8001:
            # sessions: size(u32) + one session: sessionHandle(u32), nonce(u16 len + bytes), attributes(u8), hmac(u16 len + bytes)
            nonce = _rand_bytes(rng, 8)
            hmac = _rand_bytes(rng, 8)
            sess = (
                _be32(0x02000000)
                + _be16(len(nonce)) + nonce
                + bytes([rng.randrange(0, 256)])
                + _be16(len(hmac)) + hmac
            )
            session_area = _be32(len(sess)) + sess
        else:
            session_area = _be32(0)
        params = handles + session_area
    elif cc == 0x00000131:  # ReadPublic: handle area with object handle
        handle = rng.randrange(0x81000000, 0x81000000 + 16)  # persistent range
        handles = _be32(handle)
        if tag == 0x8001:
            session_area = _be32(0)  # no sessions
        else:
            session_area = b""
        params = handles + session_area
    else:
        params = b""

    # Assemble header: tag(2) + size(4) + commandCode(4)
    total_len = 2 + 4 + 4 + len(params)
    if total_len > max_size:
        # trim params
        trim = total_len - max_size
        if trim >= len(params):
            params = b""
        else:
            params = params[:-trim]
        total_len = 2 + 4 + 4 + len(params)
    header = _be16(tag) + _be32(total_len) + _be32(cc)
    return header + params


def _maybe_hash_data_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Produce occasional small blobs (including empty) suitable for TPM_IO_Hash_Data
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.15:
        return b""  # empty chunk valid
    elif choice < 0.45:
        return _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(1, 64))
    else:
        return _rand_bytes(rng, rng.randint(65, 256))


def _maybe_state_blob(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # State blobs are opaque; provide small to moderate sized random data
    length = rng.choice([0, rng.randint(1, 64), rng.randint(65, 512)])
    return _rand_bytes(rng, length)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide what to generate with weighted probabilities:
    # - 60%: Valid TPM command (favoring TPMLIB_Process)
    # - 20%: Raw hash data chunk
    # - 20%: Opaque state blob
    mode = rng.random()

    max_total = 2048  # cap for TPMLIB_Process stub

    if mode < 0.6:
        # Build either TPM 1.2 or TPM 2.0 command
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            blob = _build_tpm12_command(rng, max_total)
        else:
            blob = _build_tpm20_command(rng, max_total)
        # Occasionally append benign padding that some commands ignore (rare); avoid exceeding cap
        if rng.random() < 0.1:
            pad_len = rng.randint(0, max(0, max_total - len(blob)))
            blob += _rand_bytes(rng, pad_len)
            # Fix length field if we appended padding to a command: we should not; thus only append when 0.
            # To keep validity, do not modify header lengths; thus constrain pad_len to 0.
            # Correct behavior: disable padding
            blob = blob[:len(blob) - pad_len]
        return blob
    elif mode < 0.8:
        return _maybe_hash_data_blob(rng)
    else:
        blob = _maybe_state_blob(rng)
        # Ensure <= 2048 for safety
        return blob[:2048]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets TPMLIB_DecodeBlob which expects an ASCII-armored blob
# with BEGIN/END tags for a given blob type. From the enum TPMLIB_BlobType in
# the provided headers, only TPMLIB_BLOB_TYPE_INITSTATE is currently defined.
# We therefore generate valid armored blocks for INITSTATE, with variability
# in payload length, line wrapping, and optional noise around the blob.
# The fuzzer stub picks a type in [0, TPMLIB_BLOB_TYPE_LAST), so we emit the
# INITSTATE tags to maximize valid decodes when the random choice matches.

# Armor tags commonly used by libtpms for initstate (per documentation patterns):
BEGIN_TAG_INIT = "-----BEGIN LIBTPMS INITSTATE-----"
END_TAG_INIT = "-----END LIBTPMS INITSTATE-----"

# A simple Base64 encoder using standard alphabet without external deps.
# We avoid importing base64 to keep full control over line wrapping.
_B64_ALPH = b"ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789+/"

def _b64_encode(data: bytes) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    # process 3-byte chunks
    for i in range(0, len(data), 3):
        chunk = data[i:i+3]
        pad = 3 - len(chunk)
        b = int.from_bytes(chunk.ljust(3, b"\0"), "big")
        idx0 = (b >> 18) & 0x3F
        idx1 = (b >> 12) & 0x3F
        idx2 = (b >> 6) & 0x3F
        idx3 = b & 0x3F
        out.append(_B64_ALPH[idx0])
        out.append(_B64_ALPH[idx1])
        out.append(_B64_ALPH[idx2] if pad < 2 else ord('='))
        out.append(_B64_ALPH[idx3] if pad < 1 else ord('='))
    return bytes(out)


def _wrap_lines(b: bytes, width: int) -> bytes:
    if width <= 0:
        return b
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    for i in range(0, len(b), width):
        lines.append(b[i:i+width])
    return b"\n".join(lines)


def _rand_ascii_noise(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    # Printable ASCII including whitespace except NUL; include some newlines
    printable = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + " "
    s = []
    for _ in range(length):
        if rng.random() < 0.08:
            s.append("\n")
        else:
            s.append(rng.choice(printable))
    return "".join(s)


def _generate_initstate_blob(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Generate a plausible binary payload. Since we don't know real format,
    # produce structured-looking data with recognizable headers to exercise parser.
    # Keep size small to fit under 4096 when armored.
    # Choose payload length between 16 and 1024 bytes.
    payload_len = rng.randint(16, 1024)

    # Build pseudo-structured payload: magic + version + sections
    magic = b"TPMS"  # 4 bytes magic
    version = rng.randrange(0, 5).to_bytes(1, 'big')  # 1 byte version
    flags = rng.getrandbits(16).to_bytes(2, 'big')    # 2 bytes flags
    section_count = rng.randrange(1, 6)
    header = magic + version + flags + section_count.to_bytes(1, 'big')

    body = bytearray()
    # Create sections: type(1) + len(2) + data
    remaining = max(0, payload_len - len(header))
    for i in range(section_count):
        if remaining <= 3:
            break
        stype = rng.randrange(0, 256)
        # allocate between 0 and remaining-3 for data
        max_data = max(0, remaining - 3)
        dlen = rng.randrange(0, min(128, max_data) + 1)
        data = rng.randbytes(dlen)
        body += bytes([stype]) + dlen.to_bytes(2, 'big') + data
        remaining -= 3 + dlen

    # If we still need to fill to payload_len, pad with random bytes
    if len(header) + len(body) < payload_len:
        body += rng.randbytes(payload_len - (len(header) + len(body)))

    payload = bytes(header) + bytes(body)

    # Base64 encode with optional line wrapping between 48 and 76 chars
    b64 = _b64_encode(payload)
    wrap = rng.choice([48, 64, 76])
    b64_wrapped = _wrap_lines(b64, wrap)

    # Optional headers/footers in armor (key=value style)
    kv_lines = []
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        kv_lines.append(f"Version: {1 + rng.randrange(0,3)}")
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        kv_lines.append(f"Comment: {_rand_ascii_noise(rng, rng.randrange(5, 20))}")

    parts = [BEGIN_TAG_INIT]
    if kv_lines:
        parts.extend(kv_lines)
    parts.append("")  # blank line before b64
    parts.append(b64_wrapped.decode('ascii'))
    parts.append(END_TAG_INIT)

    blob = "\n".join(parts)
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide to emit exactly one valid INITSTATE armor, possibly with benign noise
    blob = _generate_initstate_blob(rng)

    # Optionally surround with noise that should be ignored by strict decoders
    # but still present as ASCII. Keep size under 4096.
    prefix = ""
    suffix = ""
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        prefix = _rand_ascii_noise(rng, rng.randrange(0, 100)) + "\n"
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        suffix = "\n" + _rand_ascii_noise(rng, rng.randrange(0, 100))

    s = prefix + blob + suffix

    # Ensure under 4096 bytes; if too large, trim noise first, then reduce b64 lines
    b = s.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # Remove noise
        s = blob
        b = s.encode('ascii')
    if len(b) > 4096:
        # As a last resort, rebuild with smaller payload
        rng_small = random.Random(seed ^ 0xA5A55A5A)
        def small_blob() -> str:
            # minimal payload
            magic = b"TPMS"
            version = (0).to_bytes(1, 'big')
            flags = (0).to_bytes(2, 'big')
            header = magic + version + flags + (1).to_bytes(1, 'big')
            body = bytes([0]) + (0).to_bytes(2, 'big')
            payload = header + body
            b64 = _wrap_lines(_b64_encode(payload), 64).decode('ascii')
            return "\n".join([BEGIN_TAG_INIT, "", b64, END_TAG_INIT])
        s = small_blob()
        b = s.encode('ascii')

    return b

import base64
import random
import string
from typing import Tuple

# This generator creates an ASCII-armored blob suitable for TPMLIB_DecodeBlob
# The fuzzer stub chooses a TPMLIB_BlobType within [0, TPMLIB_BLOB_TYPE_LAST).
# From the provided enums, only TPMLIB_BLOB_TYPE_INITSTATE is a valid concrete type.
# The decoder expects something like:
#   -----BEGIN LIBTPMS INITSTATE-----\n
#   <base64 body possibly split in lines>\n
#   -----END LIBTPMS INITSTATE-----\n
# It may also accept optional headers; we include a few benign variations while
# keeping the blob valid so it is likely decoded successfully.

MAX_SIZE = 4096
LINE_WRAP_CHOICES = [0, 32, 48, 64, 76]  # 0 means no line breaks

BEGIN_TAG = "-----BEGIN LIBTPMS INITSTATE-----"
END_TAG = "-----END LIBTPMS INITSTATE-----"


def _rand_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _wrap_lines(b64: str, width: int) -> str:
    if width <= 0:
        return b64
    return "\n".join(b64[i:i + width] for i in range(0, len(b64), width))


def _maybe_headers(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Some decoders tolerate simple header lines before the body.
    # Keep them simple ASCII and short.
    headers = []
    # 0-3 headers
    for _ in range(rng.randrange(0, 4)):
        key_len = rng.randrange(3, 12)
        val_len = rng.randrange(0, 16)
        key = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_uppercase + string.digits) for _ in range(key_len))
        val = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + '+/=_-') for _ in range(val_len))
        if val:
            headers.append(f"{key}: {val}")
        else:
            headers.append(f"{key}:")
    return "\n".join(headers) + ("\n" if headers else "")


def _choose_payload_size(rng: random.Random) -> int:
    # Favor a range of sizes including small and moderately large, but cap so final text <= MAX_SIZE
    # Base64 expands by 4/3 plus line breaks and tags; keep margin.
    # Tags and headers cost < 256 bytes typically; keep binary payload <= 2048.
    choices = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, 128, 192, 256, 384, 512, 768, 1024, 1536, 2048]
    size = rng.choice(choices)
    # Occasionally pick a random value within [5, 1500]
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        size = rng.randrange(5, 1501)
    return size


def _make_valid_blob(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    payload_len = _choose_payload_size(rng)
    payload = _rand_bytes(rng, payload_len)

    # Occasionally craft payloads with interesting binary patterns
    if payload_len > 0 and rng.random() < 0.3:
        patterns = [
            b"\x00" * payload_len,
            b"\xff" * payload_len,
            (b"\x00\xff" * (payload_len // 2)) + (b"\x00" if payload_len % 2 else b""),
            bytes([i % 256 for i in range(payload_len)]),
        ]
        payload = rng.choice(patterns)

    b64 = base64.b64encode(payload).decode('ascii')

    # Optionally add a newline every N chars
    wrap = rng.choice(LINE_WRAP_CHOICES)
    body = _wrap_lines(b64, wrap)

    headers = _maybe_headers(rng)

    # Optionally add blank lines around body
    pre_blank = "\n" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""
    post_blank = "\n" if rng.random() < 0.5 else ""

    parts = [BEGIN_TAG, "\n"]
    if headers:
        parts.append(headers)
    parts.append(pre_blank)
    parts.append(body)
    parts.append(post_blank)
    parts.append("\n")
    parts.append(END_TAG)
    parts.append("\n")

    text = "".join(parts)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(text.encode('ascii')) > MAX_SIZE:
        # If exceeded due to line wrapping or headers, reduce payload and regenerate simply
        simple_b64 = base64.b64encode(payload[:128]).decode('ascii')
        text = f"{BEGIN_TAG}\n{simple_b64}\n{END_TAG}\n"
    return text


def _maybe_variants(rng: random.Random, text: str) -> str:
    # Introduce valid variations that should still parse:
    # - Trailing whitespace lines
    # - Extra newlines at end
    # Avoid corrupting tags or base64 body content.
    variant = text
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        variant = variant + ("\n" * rng.randrange(1, 3))
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        # add harmless spaces on blank lines between body and END
        variant = variant.replace("\n\n" + END_TAG, "\n \n" + END_TAG)
    return variant


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create a valid INITSTATE blob. The fuzzer stub will sometimes select this type.
    text = _make_valid_blob(rng)
    text = _maybe_variants(rng, text)

    data = text.encode('ascii')
    if len(data) > MAX_SIZE:
        data = data[:MAX_SIZE]
    return data

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces a valid UTF-8, NUL-terminated byte string suitable
# for TPMLIB_SetDebugPrefix and TPMLIB_SetProfile, aiming to cover interesting
# cases: empty, ASCII, long, mixed Unicode, combining marks, RTL/LTR marks,
# emoji, edge plane characters, and strings resembling profile names.

MAX_TOTAL = 4096

ASCII = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " _-.:/\"'[]{}()+,;@#%$!^&~`|?"

# Some interesting Unicode code point ranges and specific characters
UNICODE_BLOCKS = [
    # Latin-1 Supplement
    (0x00A0, 0x00FF),
    # Latin Extended-A
    (0x0100, 0x017F),
    # Greek and Coptic
    (0x0370, 0x03FF),
    # Cyrillic
    (0x0400, 0x04FF),
    # Hebrew
    (0x0590, 0x05FF),
    # Arabic
    (0x0600, 0x06FF),
    # Devanagari
    (0x0900, 0x097F),
    # CJK Unified Ideographs (sample subset)
    (0x4E00, 0x4F80),
    # Hangul Syllables (sample subset)
    (0xAC00, 0xACFF),
]

COMBINING_MARKS = [
    0x0301,  # COMBINING ACUTE ACCENT
    0x0308,  # COMBINING DIAERESIS
    0x0300,  # COMBINING GRAVE ACCENT
    0x0327,  # COMBINING CEDILLA
]

SPECIALS = [
    0x200B,  # ZERO WIDTH SPACE
    0x200D,  # ZERO WIDTH JOINER
    0x200C,  # ZERO WIDTH NON-JOINER
    0x202A,  # LRE
    0x202B,  # RLE
    0x202C,  # PDF
    0x2066,  # LRI
    0x2067,  # RLI
    0x2069,  # PDI
]

EMOJI = [
    0x1F600,  # 😀
    0x1F602,  # 😂
    0x1F680,  # 🚀
    0x1F4A9,  # 💩
    0x1F512,  # 🔒
    0x1F511,  # 🔑
    0x1F3AF,  # 🎯
]

# Some plausible profile-like tokens
PROFILE_TOKENS = [
    "default", "strict", "compat", "tpm12", "tpm2", "fips", "oemA", "oemB",
    "test", "debug", "release", "minimal", "maximal", "nv-heavy", "ek-srk",
]

PREFIX_TOKENS = [
    "tpms", "libtpms", "tpm", "sim", "vm", "host", "guest", "qemu",
    "prefix", "log", "audit", "trace", "dbg",
]

SEPARATORS = ["-", ":", "/", ".", "_"]


def _rand_ascii(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    return ''.join(rng.choice(ASCII) for _ in range(n))


def _rand_codepoint_from_ranges(rng: random.Random, ranges: List[tuple]) -> int:
    start, end = rng.choice(ranges)
    return rng.randint(start, end)


def _rand_unicode_str(rng: random.Random, min_len: int, max_len: int) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    s = []
    for _ in range(n):
        choice = rng.random()
        if choice < 0.55:
            s.append(chr(_rand_codepoint_from_ranges(rng, UNICODE_BLOCKS)))
        elif choice < 0.75:
            s.append(chr(rng.choice(EMOJI)))
        elif choice < 0.9:
            base = chr(_rand_codepoint_from_ranges(rng, UNICODE_BLOCKS))
            marks = ''.join(chr(rng.choice(COMBINING_MARKS)) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 2)))
            s.append(base + marks)
        else:
            s.append(chr(rng.choice(SPECIALS)))
    return ''.join(s)


def _profile_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build something like: vendor/tpm2:strict.debug-ä🚀
    parts = []
    parts.append(rng.choice(PROFILE_TOKENS))
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(rng.choice(SEPARATORS))
        parts.append(rng.choice(PROFILE_TOKENS))
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        parts.append(rng.choice(SEPARATORS))
        parts.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 3, 8))
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        parts.append(rng.choice(SEPARATORS))
        parts.append(_rand_unicode_str(rng, 1, 3))
    return ''.join(parts)


def _prefix_like(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build something like: [qemu-tpm] or tpm:sim-线程
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        core = rng.choice(PREFIX_TOKENS)
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            core += rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + rng.choice(PREFIX_TOKENS)
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            core += rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + _rand_ascii(rng, 1, 4)
        if rng.random() < 0.4:
            core += rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + _rand_unicode_str(rng, 1, 2)
        return core
    else:
        # Bracketed style
        inner = _profile_like(rng)
        return f"[{inner}]"


def _pick_case(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    cases = []
    # Empty string
    cases.append("")
    # Short ASCII
    cases.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 1, 12))
    # Long ASCII within reasonable limit
    cases.append(_rand_ascii(rng, 64, 256))
    # Mixed Unicode
    cases.append(_rand_unicode_str(rng, 8, 48))
    # Emoji heavy
    cases.append(''.join(chr(rng.choice(EMOJI)) for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 16))))
    # RTL/LTR markers wrapped around text
    rtl = "\u202B" + _rand_unicode_str(rng, 4, 12) + "\u202C"
    ltr = "\u202A" + _rand_unicode_str(rng, 4, 12) + "\u202C"
    cases.append(rng.choice([rtl, ltr]))
    # Profile-like and prefix-like
    cases.append(_profile_like(rng))
    cases.append(_prefix_like(rng))
    # Combination of tokens
    combo = rng.choice(PREFIX_TOKENS) + rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + rng.choice(PROFILE_TOKENS)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        combo += rng.choice(SEPARATORS) + _rand_unicode_str(rng, 1, 3)
    cases.append(combo)
    return rng.choice(cases)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose one or two strings and optionally concatenate to create variety
    s1 = _pick_case(rng)
    if rng.random() < 0.35:
        sep = rng.choice([" ", rng.choice(SEPARATORS)])
        s2 = _pick_case(rng)
        s = s1 + sep + s2
    else:
        s = s1

    # Clamp to ensure space for trailing NUL and overall size limit
    # Ensure at least one character sometimes for non-empty cases
    max_payload = max(0, min(MAX_TOTAL - 1, 1024))  # keep it small but safe
    enc = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    if len(enc) > max_payload:
        # Truncate by code points to avoid cutting within a multi-byte sequence
        truncated = []
        total = 0
        for ch in s:
            b = ch.encode('utf-8')
            if total + len(b) > max_payload:
                break
            truncated.append(ch)
            total += len(b)
        enc = ''.join(truncated).encode('utf-8')

    # Append NUL terminator because the C API expects NUL-terminated strings
    return enc + b"\x00"
